strings.title: KEY_MIRROR
strings.subtitle: Skill: joining two tables
strings.briefing:
Two tables describe the same business. orders knows what was bought and the customer's id. customers knows who each id belongs to. Neither has the whole story.

Join them so every order carries its customer_name and city, and no order is lost along the way.

In Python, df holds the orders and customers holds the people; finish with df as the combined table. In SQL, data holds the orders and customers the people; build a table named result and that is what gets judged.
strings.task: Combine the orders with the customers table so every order also shows its customer_name and city. Keep all 120 orders.

python: A join needs a key both tables share. Here it is customer_id.
Use df.merge(customers, on='customer_id', how='left'). A left join keeps every row of df.
sql: The key both tables share is customer_id. Use a LEFT JOIN so every order stays.
CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT ... FROM data d LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = d.customer_id;
CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT d.*, c.customer_name, c.city FROM data d LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = d.customer_id;
